_doc: Campaigns: an ordered list of chapters (maps). Heroes listed in 'heroes' are the campaign's veterans: they are matched by id to the heroes of each chapter map and keep level, XP, primaries, skills, unspent points, marks and their artifacts between chapters: with carry.keep_worn everything worn plus up to carry.max_artifacts from the pack, otherwise up to carry.max_artifacts in all (armies and resources do not carry over). Each chapter's level_cap holds hero levels back on that map (XP keeps accruing and pays out when a later chapter raises the cap), which paces a campaign at roughly 1-3 levels per map. start_resources are added to the human player at the start of the chapter. rewards are granted on victory: xp to every veteran, artifact to the first veteran listed. Optional per chapter: max_tier (the highest creature tier any town on the map may build or recruit; must not fall from chapter to chapter; 0 or absent = no limit), ai (StrategicAI setting overrides for every computer player, e.g. {"passive": true} for a tutorial opponent that never attacks the player), setup (GameSetup players: faction and human/computer per map slot), cast (heroes placed on the map: [{id, name, class, owner, army, replaces?}]; how a generated map, "gen:<template>:<seed>", gets the campaign veterans: "replaces" takes a generated hero's place, others stand next to their owner's first hero), intro (the briefing story; paragraphs separated by a blank line; falls back to text) and outro (story shown on victory), take_artifacts (artifact ids the story takes from the veterans when the chapter starts, worn or packed; they do not come back) and scenario (ScenarioRules objectives for the chapter map; a hand-made map's own "scenario" key is used when the chapter has none). See src/game/campaign.gd.

last_light.name: The Last Light
last_light.text: The dead rise in the south, the sky turns red and a hundred-year-old seal is breaking. Sir Aldous Wren of Greyhold learns why no one comes when the Concord calls. Chapter 1 is the tutorial; chapters 8 to 10 are the old Ember Chronicle.

chapters.name: Greyhold Harvest
chapters.text: The dead are crawling out of the barrow fields at harvest. Clear them from Greyhold's land.
chapters.intro:
Harvest in the southern marches, and the barrow fields are moving. Shamblers have dug themselves out of the old graves east of Greyhold and made a camp in the fen. Sir Aldous Wren, the town's lord, rides out with what men he has.

How to play: click a tile to plan Aldous's route, then click it again to march. Walk onto the sawmill and the ore pit to claim them, and pick up the piles on the way. Open Greyhold (T) to build and recruit. Each building costs resources and you can build once a day. Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2 here. When you are ready, attack the rats in the grain: the forecast shows your odds before you commit. Then take Barrow Camp. Press E to end the day.

The dead here will not come to you. Take your time.
chapters.outro: The barrow camp burns. The dead it held were fresh: farmers buried this summer, and others that no one in Greyhold remembers burying at all. The ground in the barrow fields is warm to the touch.

chapters.name: The Barrow Roads
chapters.text: The dead march up the old roads in columns. Burn the barrows that send them.
chapters.intro:
Every barrow along the south road has opened. The dead march north in columns, too orderly for corpses. Maelis Thorne, Wren's ranger captain, has tracked them to a single grave-town, kept by a gravedigger called Sexton Grue who buried half of them himself.

Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 3. Break the dead and take their town.
chapters.outro: The grave-town falls, but the columns came from somewhere further south, where the fens begin.

chapters.name: Lanterns in the Fen
chapters.text: A lantern-priest joins the march and says the ground itself is warm.
chapters.intro:
Sister Edda Vey of the lantern temples joins the march with a lamp that burns blue near the dead. She says the warmth in the ground is not the summer. Something deep below is waking, and the dead are only the first to feel it.

Edda is an Oracle: she sees far and learns fast. The Hollow town that guards the fen road is held by Father Corvin Mire, who was a lantern-priest once; Edda knew him. Hold the fen road and take his town.
chapters.outro: Edda reads the ash in the lamp and goes pale. "Not something waking," she says. "Something leaking."

objectives.text: Take Fenlight from the dead.
Drive Father Corvin Mire off the Fen Road.

chapters.name: The Knight Who Came Back
chapters.text: The dead are led by a knight in the colours of House Wren.
chapters.intro:
Scouts come back from the fens with a name no one wants to say. The dead are led by a knight on a gibbet-horse, in the faded colours of House Wren. Sir Orrin Wren died a hundred years ago holding the gate shut against the Ashen Host. His great-grandson now has to cut him down.

Orrin rides with gibbet knights, which are far stronger than anything you can raise yet (tier 4). Retake Fenwick, cross the dikes and break Saint Orrin's Rest.
chapters.outro: Orrin falls in the chapel yard. Before the light leaves his eyes he grips Aldous's wrist. "The stone is cracking, boy. They will not tell you. Go to the mountain."

chapters.name: Doors of Stone
chapters.text: The Forge cast the Lockstone. Wren rides to its gates for help.
chapters.intro:
The Lockstone, the seal on the Wound, was cast by the Sunken Forge, and the Concord stopped paying for its upkeep forty years ago. Aldous rides to the mountain gates with Orrin's warning. The gates stay shut. Then the border wardens march out under Ironmarshal Dask Vell to drive off the "debtors".

Tier 5 is open: lantern priests heal your army. Break the wardens' hold.
chapters.outro: The wardens fall back behind the rock. From the walls a runesmith shouts down: "You owe us forty years. Pay it in your own blood." The gates do not open.

objectives.text: Keep Tobbin Greave's workshop standing.
Break the Border Wardens and take the Mountain Gate.

chapters.name: The Stumps of Elderwold
chapters.text: The road to the Wound runs through the forest the Concord cut down.
chapters.intro:
The short road to the Wound runs through Elderwold, the forest the Concord felled to feed its foundries. Nothing grows there now but stumps and thorn. The Thornwood Covenant has not forgotten, and its huntmaster, Neve Hollowreed, has had archers in the stumps for a week.

Maelis was born in this forest. She is quiet the whole way in. Take the Covenant's towns before their archers take your army apart.
chapters.outro: A dying druid tells Maelis what the forest knew: the great roots of Elderwold held the Lockstone in place. When the Concord cut the trees, it cut the seal. Before he dies the druid looks at Maelis and calls her Branwen. She does not answer to it, and she does not tell Aldous any of it for a day.

objectives.text: Bring Aldous Wren to the living grove at the eastern edge of the stumps by day 24.
Take the Covenant groves of Neve Hollowreed.

chapters.name: Raiders under a Red Sky
chapters.text: The sky turns red. Starving clans raid the north while the army is away.
chapters.intro:
One morning the sky is red and stays red. Ash falls like snow. Word comes from the north: the Frostmarch clans are over the border under a reaver called Bjarr Coldhand, burning granaries. Their summer never came, and the Concord stopped sending grain long ago.

Tier 6 is open: sunhawk riders. The clans are fast and many. Drive them back over the border.
chapters.outro: The last raider dies laughing. "Your sky did this," he says. "Your fire. We are only hungry." To the south-east, beyond the ash, the horizon glows.

betrayal.text: The granaries are empty. Hrodna's clan was never full.

objectives.text: Retake the Westmere and Eastmere granaries.
Keep Clan Grimfell in the field.
Drive every raider out of the north.

chapters.name: The Burning Ford
chapters.text: The Lockstone breaks. The first Ashen army in a hundred years crosses the river.
chapters.intro:
The Lockstone has broken. For the first time in a hundred years the Ashen Host walks under the sky: slag-spawn, skinless hounds and things with hooks for arms. Its vanguard has already crossed the river at Greyhold's eastern ford.

Tier 7 is open: the bastion colossus. Hold the ford and break the vanguard.
chapters.outro: The vanguard is broken but it was only meant to bleed you. Behind it, the whole Host is coming out of the Wound.

chapters.name: Ashes Return
chapters.text: The Host comes back in force. The Iron Margrave rides out of the last reserve.
chapters.intro:
The Host comes back across the wastes in force, and the Concord's capital sends its last reserve: the Iron Margraves, warlord-knights on barded destriers, who have not ridden to war since the Sealing.

Tier 8 is open. Every unit the Concord has is yours. Two war-leaders hold the wastes beyond the river. Break the Host's march and take both its towns.
chapters.outro: The Host breaks and falls back to its pit. Cindermaw, the fortress on the lip of the Wound, is the last thing between the Concord and the gate.

chapters.name: Into the Embers
chapters.text: Carry the war to Cindermaw and hold the gate as Orrin did.
chapters.intro:
Cindermaw sits on the lip of the Wound, behind a ridge with two passes. Skarn Ashborn holds it with everything the Host has left. Beyond it, the gate stands open.

Take Cindermaw and Pyrehold. Hold the gate as your great-grandfather did.
chapters.outro: Aldous Wren stands where Orrin stood a hundred years ago, and the gate does not close. It cannot be closed by soldiers alone. The Concord will have to ask the peoples it wronged, and this time it will have to pay.

pale_inheritance.name: The Pale Inheritance
pale_inheritance.text: The dead are not rising to serve the demons. They are fleeing them. Ysmay Vane, the Unburied Regent of Sallowmere, turns their terror into a kingdom.

chapters.name: The Warm Earth
chapters.text: The dead wake by the thousand in Sallowmere. A barrow-lord will not kneel to the Regent.
chapters.intro:
For three hundred years Ysmay Vane has ruled the fens of Sallowmere from a throne no one else wanted: a dwindling court of the dead, too few to matter. This autumn the ground is warm, and the dead are waking by the thousand. They crawl up out of the mud as if something below were chasing them.

A court that grows can be a kingdom. Ysmay sends her champion, Sir Orrin Wren, a hundred years in his grave, to tell the barrow-lords of the fen. Vathek of Cairnholt answers that he kneels to no one.

Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2. Take Cairnholt.
chapters.outro: Vathek's hill falls and his dead turn to the Regent without a word. They were never his; they were only near him. Ysmay counts what she has gained and finds the number is still rising. Every night more of the dead climb out of the fen, and none of them can say what woke them.

chapters.name: Barrow-Lords
chapters.text: Ysmay unites the fens by force, one barrow-lord at a time.
chapters.intro:
Cairnholt was the smallest of the barrow-lords. The others have heard, and they have gathered behind the oldest of them, Morrow of the Deep Fen, who was a barrow-lord before Ysmay was born. They would rather go on sleeping than serve.

Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 3: gravecrawlers. Break the barrow-lords and take their town.
chapters.outro: The last barrow-lord kneels with his jaw hanging loose. "Something is burning below," he says. "Under the fen, under the graves. We are not rising, Regent. We are fleeing." Ysmay does not answer. A frightened army still marches.

chapters.name: The Living Shore
chapters.text: The first raids on the Concord marches. Father Corvin Mire joins the Regent.
chapters.intro:
The fens are full. North of them lie the Concord's marches: farms, mills and warm bodies, and graveyards that have never been asked what they want. Father Corvin Mire, once a lantern-priest of the Concord, now a Blightcaller, comes to the Regent's court with a list of the villages that buried his flock without rites.

Corvin is a Blightcaller: rot follows him. Take the Concord town on the shore of the fen. A lantern brother, Tamsin Hale, holds it.
chapters.outro:
The town is yours and its graveyard empties into your ranks. Orrin stands a long time in front of the chapel, reading the names on the wall. One of them is his own.

Far out on the shore, Corvin's scouts report shapes standing in the surf at dusk, watching the town burn. By morning there is nothing on the sand but deep, clawed prints walking back into the sea.

objectives.text: Keep the Drowned Choir in the field.
Drive Fenwick and the Shore Levies out of the marches.

chapters.name: Rot in the Roots
chapters.text: Thornwood druids burn the edge of the fen to keep the rot from their forest.
chapters.intro:
Where the dead walk, the ground rots, and the rot is creeping north toward what is left of the Elderwold. The Thornwood Covenant has answered the only way it knows: Grovewarden Cerrid Ashbark is burning the edge of the fen, and the court's new graves with it.

Tier 4 is open: wailing shades. Drive the druids back from the fen.
chapters.outro: Cerrid escapes into the trees with half his warband. Among the ashes of a druid camp Corvin finds old carvings of a great stone held in a net of roots. "They knew," he says. "The roots held something shut, and the Concord cut them down."

objectives.text: Take the Charnel House from the druids.
Burn out Cerrid Ashbark's camp.

chapters.name: Twice Dead
chapters.text: Orrin falls to his own great-grandson. Break through Greyhold and bring his body home.
chapters.intro:
Sir Orrin Wren rode to Saint Orrin's Rest to hold it against the Concord, and the Concord sent his own great-grandson. Aldous Wren cut him down at the chapel door and carried the body back to Greyhold to burn it at dawn.

The Regent does not let go of what is hers. Tier 5 is open: corpse weavers. Cross the dike, take Greyhold and recover Orrin's body before the pyre is lit.
chapters.outro: Greyhold burns, but not Orrin. Ysmay finds him laid out in the chapel under a Concord banner, and raises him a second time before the walls have stopped smoking. He opens his eyes and asks only one thing: whether the boy lived. He did.

chapters.name: The Lantern Siege
chapters.text: A lantern temple-fortress burns the dead with holy light. It must fall.
chapters.intro:
North of the fens the lantern-priests have built a temple-fortress whose lamps burn the dead at a hundred paces. Abbess Maud Lorne keeps it, and every night the court loses whole columns to its light. Corvin served in a temple like it, once. He knows where the oil is kept.

Put out the lanterns. Take the fortress.
chapters.outro: The last lamp goes dark. In the temple vault Orrin finds a hundred years of records, among them the order that sealed the Wound: five peoples, one stone, and the roots of the Elderwold to hold it. He reads it twice, and then he says nothing at all for three days.

betrayal.text: The lanterns call the living home.

objectives.text: Keep the Fenwick Levies with the Court.
Take the Lantern Fortress.
Put out every lantern.

chapters.name: Down the Deep Barrows
chapters.text: Ysmay goes below and finds why the dead woke: Ashen burrowers in the grave-realm.
chapters.intro:
The dead keep fleeing upward, so the Regent goes down. Beneath the oldest barrows lies the Barrow Below, where the dead of the south have slept since before the Concord had a name. It is full of smoke. Something has dug into it from the east: tunnels still hot, walls scored with claws.

Tier 6 is open: gibbet knights. Find the diggers, a brood under a chief called Garsh Emberclaw, and drive them out.
chapters.outro: The diggers are Ashen: burrowers of the Host, tunnelling around the Lockstone through the land of the dead because the stone itself still holds. The dead did not wake because the world was warm. They woke because the Host was walking through their graves.

chapters.name: The Hungry Fire
chapters.text: The fire eats the old tombs. The dead fight for their own graves.
chapters.intro:
The Lockstone has broken and the whole Host is coming out. Most of it marches on the Concord. Some of it stays below, and it is burning the Barrow Below tomb by tomb. Morvath the Kindler, who remembers the Sealing, feeds the dead to his fires because he likes the smell.

Tier 7 is open: charnel hulks. Fight for the graves.
chapters.outro: Morvath's fires go out one by one. The dead who were burned do not come back: there is nothing left of them to raise. For the first time in three hundred years Ysmay Vane is afraid of something.

objectives.text: Hold the three tombs through day 28.
Put out every fire Morvath sends.

chapters.name: The Leviathan Stirs
chapters.text: A drowned colossus is raised from the deepest fen: the rotwing leviathan.
chapters.intro:
Skarn Ashborn himself has come down into the Barrow Below. The court cannot match the Host fire for fire, so the Regent reaches for the oldest thing in the fen: a winged colossus that drowned in the mire before the five peoples had names, and has been rotting there ever since.

Tier 8 is open: the rotwing leviathan. Raise it and break Skarn's host.
chapters.outro: Skarn pulls back into the deepest tunnels, where the Host has made its own towns out of the old tombs. The leviathan circles above the fen under the red sky. Ysmay watches it and begins to speak of crowns.

chapters.name: The Pale Crown
chapters.text: One against two: drive both Ashen broods out of the Barrow Below and be crowned in the open air.
chapters.intro:
Two broods of the Host hold the burning tunnels: Skarn Ashborn's Burrow-Host in the north and the brood of Ithra Sootveil, his warlock, in the south. Between them and the Regent lies the Barrow Below and the Barrow Gate, which the Host has taken for its own.

The broods do not trust each other and will fight each other as readily as you. Take the Barrow Gate, then burn both broods out of the dead's country.
chapters.outro:
The last Ashen fire in the Barrow Below goes out. Ysmay Vane climbs her mound in Sallowmere and is crowned under the red sky by the dead of three hundred years, and the living of the south do not come to stop her. The southern marches are a kingdom of the dead now.

Orrin's debt to the Regent is paid. He takes his sword and walks north toward Greyhold, to find his great-grandson. He knows something about how the Lockstone was made, and the boy will need to hear it.

unsealing.name: The Unsealing
unsealing.text: A hundred years in the Wound starved the Host and broke it into broods. Skarn Ashborn, a pit-chief with nothing, climbs out to lead it, and to burn everyone who shut it in.

chapters.name: The Pit Below
chapters.text: Skarn Ashborn takes his first pit inside the Wound.
chapters.intro:
A hundred years in the Wound. The Host that was sealed in here has eaten what there was to eat, and then it began to eat itself. It is broods now, not a Host: packs of cinderlings and hounds, each around a chief who is strong this month.

Skarn Ashborn is a pit-chief with one pit and no name worth burning. Next door, Vrask Gutmaw has a bigger pit. Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2. Take the Gnawing Pit.
chapters.outro: Vrask is eaten, as is the custom. His brood licks the ash from Skarn's claws. Two pits now. Above them, for the first time any of them can remember, the rock is warm.

chapters.name: Brood War
chapters.text: The broods kneel or burn. Ithra Sootveil joins and shows Skarn the cracks.
chapters.intro:
A warlock comes to Skarn's pit, the Gnawing Pit, uninvited. Ithra Sootveil has spent forty years with her face pressed against the Lockstone, reading its cracks the way the living read stars. "The stone is dying," she says. "Someone up there killed its roots. When it breaks, the Host walks out, and it will want one chief. Be that chief."

Ithra is a Warlock. Tier 3 is open: brimstone hurlers. Break the strongest brood in the Wound: Hrakka Ninefang's, dug in at Ninefang Hollow.
chapters.outro: Ninefang Hollow falls and the broods kneel. Ithra leads Skarn up the long shafts to the underside of the Lockstone and lays his hand on it. It is cracked through like a dropped plate, and it is hot.

chapters.name: The Wardens' Keep

objectives.text: Bring Ithra to the crack under the keep's wall
Take the Wardens' Keep

chapters.text: The Forge's old watch-keep on the Lockstone is half empty. Storm it.
chapters.intro:
The Sunken Forge built the Lockstone, and for a hundred years its wardens kept a watch-keep on the stone's edge. The Concord stopped paying for the watch. Half the keep stands empty now under a warden-captain called Bruna Kell, and the cracks run right under its walls.

Ithra knows a crack wide enough for a cinderling. Get inside and take the keep.
chapters.outro: The last warden dies at his post. In his ledger are the stone's measurements, written up every week for a hundred years. The last twenty pages say only: "Wider."

chapters.name: Under the Barrows

objectives.text: Drive the Regent and the Barrow-Lords out of the Barrow Below
Hrakka's Brood must not fall

chapters.text: Burrowers dig around the seal through the land of the dead.
chapters.intro:
The stone still holds, so the Host goes around it. Skarn's burrowers dig west, into the Barrow Below, where the dead of the south have slept for a thousand years. The dead do not like the heat. They are climbing out of their graves to get away from it, and their Regent has come down to see why.

Tier 4 is open: flayers. Drive the dead out of the tunnels.
chapters.outro: The dead pull back toward the surface. The tunnels are Skarn's. Ithra laughs for the first time in years: "Do you hear that, chief? Up there, the living are blaming their own dead for this."

chapters.name: Breaking the Lockstone
chapters.text: Lantern-priests try to reconsecrate the stone. Morvath feeds the cracks with their fire, and the Lockstone shatters.
chapters.intro:
The Concord has finally noticed. Lantern-priests have marched to the Lockstone to bless it shut again with holy fire, and their Abbess, Maud Lorne, is already singing at the stone.

Morvath the Kindler, who was there when the stone was laid, has come up from the deepest pit to watch. "Let them light their fires," he says. "Fire is ours." Morvath is a Tormentor. Tier 5 is open: ash witches. Take the Lantern Watch and Brightwater.
chapters.outro: Morvath carries the priests' own lanterns into the cracks, one after another. The Lockstone groans, then breaks in three. For the first time in a hundred years the Ashen Host walks out under the sky, and the sky turns red to greet it.

chapters.name: Kindling the Elderwold

objectives.text: Take Elderhollow
Burn the Covenant out of its last groves

chapters.text: The Host burns the stumps and the last groves of the felled forest.
chapters.intro:
The roots that held the stone came from the Elderwold. The Concord felled most of it; the stumps and the last groves still live, and the Host comes up into them without a town of its own. Ithra will not leave a single root in the ground that could hold anything shut again. The Thornwood druids, led by Cerrid Ashbark, hold Mothergrove and Briarwatch to defend what is left.

Take the abandoned Concord town of Elderhollow for a foothold, then burn the groves.
chapters.outro: The last grove goes up like a torch. Cerrid's druids scatter into the smoke, cursing the Concord as loudly as the Host. Morvath watches the fire with his hands spread toward it, like a man at a hearth.

chapters.name: The Ford
chapters.text: The Burning Ford from the Ashen side. A vanguard is only meant to bleed the enemy.
chapters.intro:
The Host's vanguard crosses the river at Greyhold's eastern ford. Skarn does not expect it to win. A vanguard is meant to find out how the living fight, and to bleed them while it does. Aldous Wren of Greyhold holds the far bank.

Tier 6 is open: gorgewings. Break Greyhold's knight.
chapters.outro: Wren falls back with his army half gone. Ithra has counted every lance and every lantern he had. "Now we know what they are," she says. "Fewer than they think."

chapters.name: Ash on the Snow

betrayal.text: Snow eats fire. Hrakka's brood goes back to the warm, and takes the Host's name with it.

objectives.text: Keep Hrakka's Brood in the field
Break the Frostmarch, and whoever stands with it

chapters.text: The Host's flank meets the clans on snow. A hard detour.
chapters.intro:
The ash the Host breathes out has blotted out the sun in the north. The Ashwinter has driven the Frostmarch clans south out of Rimehold, starving and furious, and they have run straight into the Host's flank at Cinderfast under their thane, Ulvra Kettleborn. Hrakka's brood marches beside the Host from its warren, grumbling about the cold. Snow eats fire. The Host hates it here.

Tier 7 is open: pyre titans. Break the clans and get off the snow before Hrakka's patience does.
chapters.outro: The clans scatter north, but they took a heavy toll. Morvath is still shaking the frost out of his joints when word comes from the deepest pit: something old has heard that the stone is broken, and it is climbing.

chapters.name: The Maw Wakes
chapters.text: The cinder maw crawls up from the deepest pit.
chapters.intro:
It was old when the Host was sealed. It slept through the hundred years at the bottom of the Wound, and now it has woken hungry: a cinder maw, a mouth the size of a gatehouse. It follows Skarn because Skarn walks toward food.

Tier 8 is open: the cinder maw. The Concord has gathered a relief army on the road to Highmere under its castellan, Odo Brack. Feed it to the maw.
chapters.outro: The relief army is gone. Only Highmere is left between the Host and the Concord's heartland: the eastern fortress, and behind its walls, the last of the Concord's friends.

chapters.name: The Red Sky Throne
chapters.text: One against three: Highmere, the Thornwood Covenant and the Sunken Forge. Skarn takes Highmere and is crowned on its walls.
chapters.intro:
At the end of the world, they finally came. The Thornwood Covenant has come out of the burned forest and the Sunken Forge has opened its gates, and both have marched to Highmere, the Concord's eastern fortress. Three peoples who hate each other, standing in one place because of the Host.

They are three armies with three masters, and none of them trusts the others. Take Highmere. Break the war-grove and the Forge hold. Every enemy town must fall.
chapters.outro:
Highmere burns. Skarn Ashborn climbs its walls and sits down on the battlements under a sky the color of an open wound, and the Host roars its new name for him: the Red Sky King.

Behind him, Ithra Sootveil has turned away from the burning city. She is looking south, at the dead country, where something pale is being crowned too.

briar_oath.name: The Briar Oath
briar_oath.text: The Covenant has watched the Concord fell its forest for forty years. Cerrid Ashbark goes to war for the last grove, and learns what his own druids kept quiet.

chapters.name: The Axe Line
chapters.text: Logging camps press into the last grove. Drive them out.
chapters.intro:
For forty years the Concord has cut the Elderwold for its ships and its roofs, and for forty years the Covenant has buried its trees. The great forest is stumps now, all but one grove in the west. This spring the Axeford Timber Company has built its camp at the grove's edge.

Cerrid Ashbark, Grovewarden, has stopped asking. Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2. Burn Axeford.
chapters.outro: The camp burns. Among the loggers' things Neve Hollowreed finds an order with the Concord's seal: the last grove, by summer. "Then they will come with soldiers," Cerrid says. "Let them."

chapters.name: Smoke over Elderwold
chapters.text: The Concord answers with soldiers and fire.
chapters.intro:
The Concord's answer comes in a week: soldiers, and fire. They mean to burn the grove out rather than cut it. Smoke is rising over the stumps beyond Hollowmere, and a knight called Piers Ashcombe is directing it from a palisaded fire-camp.

Tier 3 is open: briar huntresses. Break the Concord's fire-camp.
chapters.outro: The fire-camp is broken, but the smoke is still rising. Somewhere to the south the ground itself is warm, and the druids' oldest songs have started to go wrong in their mouths.

chapters.name: Ambush at the Stumps
chapters.text: The Concord's ranger captain rides into the felled forest. Cerrid knows her face.
chapters.intro:
A Concord column is marching through the stumps toward the south. Its scouts are led by a ranger captain called Maelis Thorne. Neve has a clean shot at her from the stumps, and Cerrid tells her to wait. He has seen that face before, thirty years ago, on a girl the soldiers carried off from a burning village. His sister.

Ambush the column and take its camp.
chapters.outro: Maelis gets away, as Cerrid meant her to. He does not tell Neve why. That night he carves a name into a living tree, the old way, so the forest will remember it.

chapters.name: Hunters in the Snow

objectives.text: Keep all three living groves through day 24
Break every hunting party that comes down from the north

chapters.text: Starving clans hunt the forest and burn its trees for warmth.
chapters.intro:
Snow in summer. Clans from the Frostmarch have come south through it, so hungry that they eat the deer raw and burn the living trees to keep from freezing. Their thane, Hrodna Grimfell, does not even know whose forest it is.

Tier 4 is open: rootbinders. Drive the clans out of the forest.
chapters.outro: The clans go back north into the white. One of their seers, dying, tells Neve that the summer did not fail: it was stolen. The sun went behind ash, and the ash comes from the south.

chapters.name: The Fen's Edge

objectives.text: Take Mossgate
Burn the Hollow off the fen's edge

chapters.text: Rot creeps north out of the fens. Burn the edge. Old Mother Brakka joins.
chapters.intro:
Where the dead walk, the ground rots, and the rot is creeping north out of the southern fens toward the forest. The Hollow hold Fenmarrow and the Drowned Chapel, and the fen town of Mossgate stands empty between them and the trees. Old Mother Brakka, the eldest Thornspeaker, has walked out of the deep wood for the first time in fifty years. She says the edge must burn.

Brakka is a Thornspeaker. Tier 5 is open: gloomwing strixes. Take Mossgate, burn the fen's edge and drive the dead back.
chapters.outro: The edge burns, and the dead pull back into the mist. Brakka does not watch the fire. She is looking past it, at the Wound, and her face is grey. "It is time," she says, "that I told you what the roots were for."

chapters.name: What the Roots Remember
chapters.text: Brakka reads the dead Heartroots and admits what the druids knew. The first Ashen scouts reach the forest.
chapters.intro:
In the middle of the felled forest lie the Heartroots, or what is left of them: a ring of dead stumps as wide as castles. Brakka lays her hands on them and reads what they remember. A hundred years ago five peoples sealed the Host in the Wound with a stone, and the roots of the Elderwold grew around it like a fist. When the Concord felled the forest, the fist let go.

"We knew," Brakka says. "The druids knew. We could have told them, and we let them cut." The first Ashen scouts are already at the clearing. Drive them off.
chapters.outro: The scouts are gone, but they burned the clearing on their way out. Cerrid stands among the ashes of the Heartroots for a long time. The Concord felled the forest. The Covenant let it fall.

chapters.name: Kindling

objectives.text: Put out Sootveil's Brood and the Kindlers
Clan Grimfell must not fall

chapters.text: The Host burns the stumps and the last groves.
chapters.intro:
The Lockstone has broken. The Host is out, and its warlock, Ithra Sootveil, has come to the forest with one order: burn every root that could hold anything shut again.

Tier 6 is open: spore lobbers. Save what you can.
chapters.outro: Ithra pulls back, but behind her the stumps of the Elderwold are burning from one horizon to the other. What is left of the forest is one valley, the Last Grove, and the Host knows where it is.

chapters.name: The Last Grove
chapters.text: Defend the heart of the remaining forest.
chapters.intro:
The Last Grove is a single valley of living trees, the oldest in the world. If it burns there is nothing left to grow back from. The Host is coming for it, and Morvath the Kindler, who likes the smell of burning, is leading it.

Tier 7 is open: rootbound ancients. Hold the Last Grove.
chapters.outro: The grove stands. In its heart, under the oldest tree, Brakka digs up something the size of a fist and wrapped in moss: a seed, black and warm, older than the Covenant. "The Mother's seed," she says. "We swore never to plant it."

chapters.name: Seed of the Mother

betrayal.text: We swore never to plant it. We meant it.

objectives.text: Keep the Greyhart Circle with you
Clear the way to the Wound

chapters.text: A single seed carried out of the fire wakes the wyrdthorn mother.
chapters.intro:
The seed wakes when it touches ash. Within a night it is a thing of thorns and limbs and hunger that walks on its roots: a wyrdthorn mother, the forest's own ultimate answer, the reason the old druids swore never to plant it. The Greyhart Circle, the last druids who kept that oath, march with Cerrid from Seedwatch, and they will not look at the mother.

Tier 8 is open: the wyrdthorn mother. Carry her through the Host's lines at the Ember Gate, which Garsh Emberclaw holds.
chapters.outro: The mother walks behind Cerrid like a hound. The Greyhart Circle is gone, broken at the Wound's edge for an oath Cerrid chose to break. The road to the Wound is open. Brakka says a mother's roots can bind anything, even a broken seal, if she is planted at its edge.

chapters.name: The Briar Seal
chapters.text: One against two: plant the wyrdthorn at the lip of the Wound while two Ashen broods hold it.
chapters.intro:
The Wound lies behind a ring of black rock, and two broods of the Host guard it: Ithra Sootveil's in the north and Morvath the Kindler's in the south. They are rivals and will fight each other as readily as you, but both will fight you.

Plant the wyrdthorn at the lip of the Wound so its roots can bind the edge. To do it, every brood town must fall.
chapters.outro:
The broods are scattered and the mother is planted at the lip of the Wound. Her roots go down into the fire, and the fire hisses. The forest will grow back over the Wound, too slowly to save anyone this year, but it will grow.

That night Cerrid writes a letter, the first word between the Covenant and the Concord in forty years. It is addressed to Maelis Thorne, and it begins with her real name: Branwen.

shuttered_halls.name: The Shuttered Halls
shuttered_halls.text: The Forge cast the Lockstone and was never paid for it, so it shut its gates. Gunnra Sootmantle is the only one who believes the rock will not keep the fire out.

chapters.name: Deep Shift
chapters.text: The lowest mines grow warm and the dead climb the shafts.
chapters.intro:
The Sunken Forge has kept its gates shut for forty years, since the Concord stopped paying for the Lockstone's upkeep. What happens on the surface stops at the rock: that is what the council says. But the lowest galleries of Stonevow Hold are warm this year, and last night something climbed up the shafts that had been buried.

Gunnra Sootmantle, Runesmith, goes down with Ironmarshal Dask Vell and his escort. Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2. Clear the Lower Shafts.
chapters.outro:
The dead in the shafts were Forge dead, miners from the old wars, buried deep. Gunnra lays her hand on the rock. It is warm, and the warmth is coming from the south-east, from the Wound.

Below the lowest shaft Dask finds a stair the Forge never cut, going down. Gunnra has it bricked up. There is enough coming from below this year.

chapters.name: Bones in the Seams
chapters.text: Seal the old tunnels before the dead reach the halls.
chapters.intro:
The dead are coming up through every old tunnel at once. The council orders the tunnels sealed with the dead still in them. Gunnra would rather know why they are rising, and who the dead abbot is that leads them.

Tier 3 is open: anvil guards. Break the dead's hold on the tunnels.
chapters.outro: The tunnels are sealed. In the last of them Gunnra finds her grandmother's mark cut into the wall, a rune she has only ever seen in one other place: on the drawings of the Lockstone.

chapters.name: The Debtors' Road
chapters.text: Concord envoys ask for help at the gates. The council says no, and the envoys try to force the pass.
chapters.intro:
A Concord lord, Aldous Wren of Greyhold, has come to the mountain gates asking for help against the dead. The council's answer is short: forty years of unpaid upkeep first. Wren decides to force the pass instead.

Drive the debtors off the road.
chapters.outro: Wren retreats down the mountain. From the walls a runesmith shouts after him that the Concord owes forty years. Gunnra is not shouting. She is wondering why a lord would ride all this way for help unless he was very afraid.

chapters.name: Iron for Bread
chapters.text: The clans demand trade, then raid the high passes.
chapters.intro:
The northern clans have come down to the high passes with empty carts. They will trade iron for bread, they say, at any price. The Forge has no bread to spare. Thane Ulvra Kettleborn stops asking and starts raiding.

Tier 4 is open: slag golems. Clear the passes.
chapters.outro: The clans pull back to the snow. Their thane leaves a message pinned to a gate with an axe: "Your mountain is warm. Ours is dying. Remember who was cold first."

chapters.name: Heat from Below
chapters.text: Ashen tunnels break into the deepest halls. Hiding has failed.
chapters.intro:
The Lockstone has broken. Within a week the Host's burrowers break through the floor of the deepest hall, the one the council said nothing could reach. The mountain is not a wall. It never was. The brood that came through is Garsh Emberclaw's.

Tier 5 is open: cinder engineers. Drive the burrowers back into their tunnels.
chapters.outro: The burrowers are driven back, but word comes from the east: Kharrak Hold, the Forge's oldest fortress, has fallen. Its gates were opened from the inside, by the heat.

chapters.name: The Fallen Hold
chapters.text: Kharrak Hold has fallen. Take it back. Master Tobbin Greave joins.
chapters.intro:
Kharrak Hold has fallen to the Host. One Forge-master still holds out in the valley: Master Tobbin Greave, an Artificer the council exiled for building an engine it had forbidden. He has been fighting the Host alone from his workshop for a week.

Tobbin is an Artificer. Take Kharrak Hold back, and the Host's camp at the Wound's mouth.
chapters.outro: Kharrak is retaken. Tobbin shows Gunnra the plans he was exiled for: an engine of molten iron that walks. "The council forbade it," he says. "The council is not here."

chapters.name: The Wardens' Keep
chapters.text: Retake the Forge's watch-keep on the broken Lockstone.
chapters.intro:
The Forge's old watch-keep on the Lockstone fell to the Host before the stone broke. Its last warden kept his ledger to the end. The council says it does not matter now. Gunnra needs to see the pieces of the stone with her own eyes.

Tier 6 is open: ironhoof chargers. Retake the keep.
chapters.outro: The warden's ledger is still on his table: a hundred years of measurements, and the last twenty pages say only "Wider". Gunnra looks at the broken stone and sees how it could be made again. It would need the Worldforge, and every master the Forge has.

chapters.name: Ore and Ember
chapters.text: Hold the ore roads while the forges are relit.
chapters.intro:
The Worldforge has been cold for a hundred years. To cast a new Lockstone it must be relit, and it will eat more ore in a month than the Forge mines in a year. The Host has found the ore roads, and a chief called Vrask, who has been eaten twice and come back twice, is sitting on them.

Tier 7 is open: thunder bombards. Hold the ore roads.
chapters.outro: The ore comes through. The Worldforge breathes again, and the whole mountain hums. The council, at last, has stopped saying no.

chapters.name: The Molten Engine
chapters.text: Tobbin finishes the great engine the council forbade.
chapters.intro:
Morvath the Kindler is leading the Host against the mountain himself. Tobbin's engine is finished: a walking furnace of molten iron, the thing the council exiled him for.

Tier 8 is open: the molten engine. Break Morvath's host.
chapters.outro: Morvath falls back. The engine stands steaming in the snow outside the gates, and the dwarves who forbade it come out to look at it. Inside, the new Lockstone is almost cast.

chapters.name: The Second Lockstone
chapters.text: One against two: cast a new seal in the Worldforge while the Host and the dead besiege the mountain.
chapters.intro:
The new Lockstone needs three more days in the Worldforge. Skarn Ashborn's Host is camped in the high pass, and the dead have come up the drowned shafts in the south, the Regent Ysmay Vane at their head. The two hate each other, but both want the mountain.

Hold the Worldforge and break both sieges. Every enemy town must fall.
chapters.outro:
The sieges break. The second Lockstone comes out of the Worldforge white-hot and ringing, cut with the same runes Gunnra's grandmother cut a hundred years ago.

It is too big for the Forge to carry to the Wound alone. For the first time in forty years, Gunnra Sootmantle orders the gates opened.

ashwinter.name: The Ashwinter
ashwinter.text: Ash blots out the northern sun and the summer never comes. Ulvra Kettleborn unites the clans by the axe and leads them south for bread, and finds an old promise waiting.

chapters.name: The Sun Goes Out
chapters.text: Red snow falls. The clans fight over the last herds.
chapters.intro:
In the north the summer did not come. The sky went grey, then red, and the snow that falls is the color of rust. The herds are dying on their feet. Clan Grimfell has driven the last good herd onto its own grazing and says it will kill anyone who comes for it.

Ulvra Kettleborn, Thane, comes for it. Your towns can raise creatures up to tier 2. Take Grimfell.
chapters.outro: Grimfell's thane kneels in the red snow. The herd is Ulvra's, and it will feed both clans for a month. After that there is nothing. The clans will have to go south, all of them, under one thane.

chapters.name: One Hall
chapters.text: Ulvra breaks the last clan that refuses her.
chapters.intro:
One clan still refuses to follow a Kettleborn south: Clan Whaleroad, the shaman clan, which keeps a cairn on the glacier it never speaks of. It would rather starve in its own hall than eat in someone else's.

Tier 3 is open: oathless berserkers. Break Thane Orm Whaleroad.
chapters.outro: The last clan comes into Ulvra's hall, and the Frostmarch is one people again for the first time since the Sealing. That night the skalds sing the old song of the Sealing, and Ulvra notices that nobody remembers the last verse.

chapters.name: South for Bread
chapters.text: Raid the northern granaries. Seer Iska Rime joins.
chapters.intro:
The Concord's northern granaries are full, and the Concord stopped sending grain north years ago. A young seer, Iska Rime, joins the war-band. She has been reading the ash in the snow, and she says it did not come from the sky.

Iska is a Frostcaller. Raid the granaries.
chapters.outro: The granaries burn. A Concord knight fights the clans to the last granary, and a raider laughs at him as he dies: "Your sky did this. Your fire. We are only hungry." Iska wonders if that is true.

chapters.name: The Iron Pass
chapters.text: The Forge shuts the mountain passes.
chapters.intro:
The clans asked the Forge to trade iron for bread, and the Forge shut the high passes on them. Ironmarshal Dask Vell holds them.

Tier 4 is open: tusk riders. Force the Iron Pass.
chapters.outro: The pass is open. Ulvra pins a message to the Forge's gate with her axe: "Your mountain is warm. Ours is dying. Remember who was cold first."

chapters.name: The Granary of Highmere
chapters.text: A great raid on the Concord's richest store-city.
chapters.intro:
Highmere, the Concord's eastern fortress, holds enough grain to feed the clans through any winter. Its castellan, Odo Brack, has two granary towns outside the walls and a river in front of them.

Tier 5 is open: frost shamans. Take Harrowby, Millstead and Highmere itself.
chapters.outro: The clans eat. For the first time since the sun went out, there is enough. Iska does not eat. She has climbed Highmere's tower and is looking south-east, where a column of ash is rising into the sky like smoke from a chimney.

chapters.name: Deer of the Old Wood
chapters.text: Hunting in the Covenant's forest means war with it.
chapters.intro:
South of Highmere lies what is left of the old forest, and in it are deer. The clans hunt them, and burn its trees to keep warm. The Thornwood Covenant's huntmaster, Neve Hollowreed, calls it theft.

Win the hunting grounds.
chapters.outro: Neve's hunters fall back. One of the clan seers, dying of a thorn, tells Neve the summer was stolen. Iska, listening, knows now where she must go.

chapters.name: Cold Bones
chapters.text: The dead walk across the frozen fens.
chapters.intro:
Iska's road south runs across the fens, and the fens are frozen. The dead walk on the ice. They are leaving the south as fast as the living are.

Tier 6 is open: rimeback aurochs. Cross the fens.
chapters.outro: The dead are behind the clans now. Ahead, the ash column is a wall, and the snow at its foot is black. Iska finds the last verse of the Sealing song carved on a cairn: the clans gave their winter to the seal. The cold held the fire low.

chapters.name: The Source of Winter
chapters.text: Iska follows the ash to the Wound. The Host is the reason the sun went out.
chapters.intro:
The ash comes from the Wound, where the Lockstone has broken and the Host has come out. Every breath the Host takes puts the sun out a little further. The Ashwinter is not a winter. It is smoke.

Tier 7 is open: cairn giants. Break the Host's northern flank. Ithra Sootveil, the Host's warlock, commands it.
chapters.outro: The flank breaks. Iska stands on the scorched plain and says what the old promise means: winter does not come from the north. The clans carry it. A hundred years ago they marched it into the Wound to freeze the fire. They can do it again.

chapters.name: Wyrm-Wake
chapters.text: Wake the winter wyrm from its glacier.
chapters.intro:
To carry a winter you need the heart of one. In the oldest glacier of the north sleeps a winter wyrm, older than the clans, colder than the sky. The Host has sent a brood under Garsh Emberclaw to keep it sleeping.

Tier 8 is open: the winter wyrm. Wake it and break the brood.
chapters.outro: The wyrm wakes, and where it breathes the snow comes back. The whole Frostmarch is marching south behind it. Ulvra no longer talks about bread.

chapters.name: Bring the Winter
chapters.text: One against two: march the Ashwinter into the Wound and freeze its fires.
chapters.intro:
Two broods of the Host hold the Wound: Morvath the Kindler's Wound-Keepers in the north and the Deep Broods in the south, either side of the burning chasm. They are rivals and will fight each other, but both will fight you.

March the winter into the Wound. Every brood town must fall.
chapters.outro:
The broods break, and the winter comes down into the Wound behind them. The fires bank low, as they did a hundred years ago. The clans have kept the old promise.

Whether anyone will pay them for it this time, Ulvra does not know. She sits down at the edge of the Wound in the falling snow and waits to find out.

long_watch.name: The Long Watch
long_watch.text: The year after the Red Sky. The Host is broken, not gone: seven banners of it still hold the Highmere road. Wren and Maelis hold the last watch on it.

chapters.name: The Last Watch
chapters.text: Hold Last Watch against the last seven banners of the Host. Expeditions can turn the siege.
chapters.intro:
The Host is broken and its king sits on Highmere's walls, but seven of its banners never went back into the Wound. They hold the road between Greyhold and Highmere, and the road ends at Last Watch, the castle Aldous Wren was given for holding the gate.

Reedhaven, the only town on the road still standing, has shut its gates to the Concord as well as the Host; its oathstone, the pledge it swore to Orrin a hundred years ago, lies in the drowned marsh where its people threw it. Hold Last Watch through the siege, win Reedhaven back, and make the seven banners pay for every day.
chapters.outro: The seventh banner falls. The watch fires burn through the rain, and Reedhaven opens its gates and hands Wren its oathstone, still wet from the marsh. But Northwatch and Crossingstead, the two frontier steadings, have sent no word, and their bells must still be ringing when the next host arrives.

chapters.name: Three Bells
chapters.text: Keep all three strongholds through an unpredictable siege.
chapters.intro:
Two frontier towns are the only homes still standing along the road, and there is no castle to fall back to this time. The broken banners have found a new chief, and he means to ring the bells silent one by one.

Keep every bell sounding. The land beyond the walls is wide and half-mapped; the scouts bring word of mines, ruins and a town that has lost its oath.
chapters.outro: Three bells answer each other across the ridge. Under the abandoned forge at Crossingstead the wardens uncover a stair into an old labyrinth, cut before the Concord had a name. The oathstone grows warm in Wren's hand and points inward. The passage is closing: twenty-one days.

chapters.name: The Stone Heart
chapters.text: Reach the Stone Heart before the end of day 21.
chapters.intro:
Wren takes the oathstone below while Maelis keeps the road. The labyrinth turns back on itself; its central chamber, the Stone Heart, lies somewhere inside. The patient road is longer, and a guardian older than the Host watches the shorter crossing.

Find the survey chambers, gather the lost who went down before you, and reach the Heart before the twenty-first night.
chapters.outro:
At the centre the oathstone fits into a scar in the living rock, and far above, the ridge falls silent. Wren does not know what he has shut, or opened. The road is still broken and the steadings still scarred, but the next dawn belongs to those who held the watch.

On the way up Maelis finds a carving on the stair that is not Concord work: a long-eared face, eyes closed, and under it six small hollows where stones have been pried out.

six_eyes.name: The Six Eyes
six_eyes.text: Expansion. The Umbral Court comes up from the deep to free the surface peoples from the six stones that turned them cruel, and carries the stones home. That was always the plan.

chapters.name: Below the Sky
chapters.intro:
The Umbral Court has kept the Nightgate for a thousand years without asking what it keeps. The houses have grown bored with the duty. This season House Draal has taken the Wardens' tithe-caverns, the mines that feed the Gate-Hold, and Sareth Draal says the Wardens can have them back when they can take them.

Matriarch Ulmarra, Veilseer of the Wardens, gives the taking to her youngest Dreadmarshal, Serane Nhalvor, and comes along to watch. Your hold can raise creatures up to tier 2. Take Draal's Terrace.
chapters.text: Serane Nhalvor retakes the Wardens' tithe-caverns from House Draal.
chapters.outro:
Sareth Draal kneels on the causeway with the black lake on either side. The tithe-caverns are the Wardens' again, and Ulmarra says, in front of every house that matters, that Serane will do.

Afterwards, alone, she speaks of the Long Stair, the uncut way up to the sky that no Warden has climbed since the gate was sealed. "Something is scratching at the top of it," she says. "Go and see what."

chapters.name: The Stair Goes Up
chapters.intro:
Halfway up the Long Stair the Wardens find the scratching: Forge miners, come down from Kharrak Hold through a shaft they should never have cut, blind with fear and digging deeper to get away from something. Their overseer, Halvar Kett, says there is an eye in the mountain that watches them and will not close.

Rhuvel Askai, a Nightstalker who has been to the surface before and did not like it, joins the march. Tier 3 is open: knifedancers. Clear the miners from the Stair: up from the Stair-Foot past the empty hold of Gloamwell and Kett's Lower Works to Kett's Breach Camp at the top.
chapters.text: Forge miners gone mad break into the deep; the Wardens follow the breach up.
chapters.outro:
The miners die quietly, grateful. In Kett's pack is a chart of Kharrak Hold with one chamber circled a hundred times: the arch of the Worldforge, and set in its keystone, a stone that watches.

Ulmarra reads the chart for a long time. "The surface peoples were given stones at the sealing," she says. "Six of them, one each. They were meant to be gifts. If one has turned a people cruel, the others will have too. Go up, Serane. Free them. Bring the Eyes home to be cleansed in the deep." Rhuvel asks, quietly, why the deep should be able to cleanse anything.

chapters.name: Under the Sky
chapters.intro:
The Court stands under the sky for the first time in a thousand years and has no town under it. The Forge's outer steadings are the only shelter, and Gunnra Sootmantle holds Kharrak Hold with the Eye of the Anvil in the arch above her, hammering her own miners into armour.

Take Stonebarrow for a roof, strip Coldforge and Hammerdeep for what they will give, then take Kharrak Hold and the Eye.
chapters.text: Townless under the sky, the Wardens take the Forge steadings and then Kharrak Hold for the first Eye.
chapters.outro:
The keystone comes out of the arch with the sound of a bell being cut. Gunnra Sootmantle sits down in her own soot and does not thank anyone. "I was building," she says. "I don't know what for."

The Eye of the Anvil is a dull red stone that weighs more than it should. Serane puts it in her pack and it seems to settle, like something that has found where it is going.

objectives.text: Take Stonebarrow
Take Kharrak Hold and the Eye inside it

chapters.name: The Saint's Eye
chapters.intro:
Greyhold. Aldous Wren has had three of his own villages burned for impurity since the spring, and the lantern-priests bless each fire. The Eye of the Saint sits in Saint Orrin's reliquary in the chapel, where the whole Concord comes to be looked at.

Tier 4 is open: cave lancers. From the Wardens' Camp, take Saint's Crossing on the pilgrim road, then Greyhold and the chapel.
chapters.text: The Wardens take Greyhold's chapel and the Eye of the Saint from Aldous Wren.
chapters.outro:
The reliquary opens on a jewel the colour of a dawn that never comes. Aldous Wren wakes on the chapel floor as if from a fever and asks what year it is, and then asks who burned the villages, and then stops asking.

Ulmarra, by lantern-glass from the deep: "Two. Bring them home." Rhuvel holds the two Eyes a hand apart and watches them pull at each other like lodestones. "They don't want the deep," he says. "They want each other."

chapters.name: Thorn and Mirror
chapters.intro:
The freed Concord marches with the Court. Aldous Wren says the Thornwood has gone the same way Greyhold went, and worse: Old Mother Brakka has rooted the Last Grove in a stone and the trees walk at night. The Eye of the Root is in the Heartroots, under her.

Tier 5 is open: veil adepts. Wren's lances camp in the north-east; Briarmoot in the middle of the wood is empty. Hold the alliance together and take the Last Grove in the south.
chapters.text: The freed Concord marches with the Court against the Thornwood, then turns at the Heartroots.
chapters.outro:
Brakka's seed had grown around the Eye of the Root for a hundred years; it comes free with half the Heartroots clinging to it, a green stone with something moving inside.

And Aldous Wren, at the edge of the grove, turns his lances on the Court. Serane cannot understand it and Ulmarra explains it: "The Eye's grip does not let go all at once. He has relapsed. Hold the Grove." Rhuvel notes that Wren did not look like a man relapsing. He looked like a man who had understood something.

betrayal.text: Wren's lances wheel. 'The Eye's grip does not let go all at once,' says Ulmarra. Hold the Grove.

objectives.text: Keep Greyhold's Lances with you
Take the Last Grove, and hold it
Break the Thornwood, and whoever stands with it

chapters.name: The Regent's Price
chapters.intro:
Ysmay Vane, Regent of the Pale Inheritance, wears the Eye of the Regent on a chain and is not turned by it, because she says she was never anything but what she is. She will not be freed. She will sell. Her price: the Red Sky King's leftover brood in the Barrow Below, two brood-camps under Garsh Emberclaw and Grisk Hollowbrand that have been eating her dead.

Fight beside the Hollow from Ysmay's Barrow and clear both broods: Emberclaw's Pit in the north-west and Hollowbrand's Pit in the south-west. The Regent's Mound in the middle is hers; leave it, or take it if the dead cannot hold it.
chapters.text: Two against two: the Court and Ysmay's Hollow break the last Ashen broods for the Eye of the Regent.
chapters.outro:
Ysmay hands over the Eye on its chain without ceremony, a grey stone that makes the hand that holds it feel watched.

"I have met your Matriarch," she says to Serane, pleasantly. "Three hundred years ago, under another name, in a house that is supposed to be extinct. Do give her my regards." Serane says her Matriarch is called Ulmarra. "Of course she is," says Ysmay.

objectives.text: Burn out both broods
The Pale Inheritance must not fall

chapters.name: Red Sky, Black Teeth
chapters.intro:
Cindermaw. Skarn Ashborn, the Red Sky King, keeps the Eye of Embers on a chain of teeth, a trophy from Highmere's treasury, and laughs when told it has turned him. "Turned me into what? I was this before I had it." He is the only enemy in this war who tells the truth, and he will not give it up.

Tier 6 is open: silk stalkers. Ashgap and Smokewell on the corners are his outworks, abandoned since the war; take them or go around. Take Cindermaw.
chapters.text: The Wardens take Cindermaw and the Eye of Embers from Skarn Ashborn.
chapters.outro:
Skarn Ashborn dies with his teeth bared and the Eye of Embers in his fist, and it has to be pried out. It is hot.

Five Eyes. Rhuvel lays them in a row in the ash and they turn, slowly, each toward the next, like a word being spelled. Ulmarra by lantern-glass: "One more. The glacier. Bring them home." Serane says she has begun to hear the word home the way Rhuvel hears it.

objectives.text: Take Cindermaw from Skarn

chapters.name: The Winter's Eye
chapters.intro:
The Ancient Glacier. The Eye of Winter is frozen into the cairn of the winter wyrm, and Ulvra Kettleborn, Thane of all the clans, has been feeding her own clans to it, a hall at a time, to keep it asleep. She says the wyrm is the only thing keeping the north alive. She may be right.

Tier 7 is open: obsidian guards. Rimegate and Whitecairn are empty of all but the dead. Take Kettlehall; the cairn is under it.
chapters.text: The Wardens break Kettlehall and take the sixth Eye from the winter wyrm's cairn.
chapters.outro:
The ice around the cairn cracks when the sixth Eye comes out, and the wyrm underneath does not wake, and Ulvra Kettleborn, freed, weeps for her halls.

Six Eyes. They do not pull at each other now. They lie still, and point, all six, the same way: down. Rhuvel: "Five of them looked at us the same way, Serane. The people who held them were not turned. They were afraid of us." Ulmarra: "Come home. The door is open."

chapters.name: The Long Stair Down
chapters.intro:
Every freed people is on the Court's heels: the Concord under Wren, the Forge under Gunnra Sootmantle, the clans under Ulvra Kettleborn, allied for the first time in a hundred years and not saying why. The Wardens hold the Stair-Hold at the top of the Long Stair with six Eyes in a box, waiting for Ulmarra's door to open below.

Tier 8 is open: gloam drakes. Greyhold's siege camp, Kharrak's forward hold and Kettlehall's winter camp close in from three corners, and the Stair-Head in the middle belongs to whoever takes it. Hold the Stair-Hold for three weeks, until the door opens.
chapters.text: Survival: the Wardens hold the Stair-Hold against three freed peoples until Ulmarra opens the way down.
chapters.outro:
The door opens. The Wardens go down the Long Stair with the six Eyes and the surface peoples do not follow past the first turning; they stand at the top in the daylight and watch, and Wren calls down the Stair, once, "Don't let her set them."

Serane asks Rhuvel what he thinks that meant. Rhuvel says he thinks they are about to find out.

objectives.text: Survive until the end of day 21
Hold the Stair-Hold

chapters.name: The Nightgate
chapters.intro:
There is no town below the Stair and no way back up it. Ulmarra takes the box with a smile Serane has seen before, in chapter one, on the causeway, and sets the six Eyes into the six sockets of the Nightgate, and says the name of House Vexmire, the house that remembers the sky, which was never extinct, which was a vow, and had members in every house, and has them now in hers.

The silver in Karzhaloth's eye-sockets cracks. Serane and Rhuvel have what they carry and no more. Break the gate-hold, kill the Matriarch, and reach the Nightgate before the dragon is fully awake.
chapters.text: Hero-only finale: Ulmarra is Vexmire; Serane and Rhuvel fight the gate-hold and then the ancient dragon.
chapters.outro:
Karzhaloth falls across the Nightgate with the six Eyes going dark in its skull one by one, and the gate stays shut, because a dragon is lying in it.

Serane Nhalvor sits down on the stair with Rhuvel and the dead Matriarch and the dead dragon, and understands that every thing she did this year was asked of her, and done well, and wrong. In the spring she climbs the Long Stair again, alone, without an army, to tell six peoples what the Court did and what it will owe them. Rhuvel goes with her. He says he has been to the surface before, and did not like it, and is going anyway.

drowned_oath.name: The Drowned Oath
drowned_oath.text: Expansion. The fish-folk of the drowned coast learn what they were and who made them what they are, and march north for revenge on a dead man, in borrowed iron, through a land that does not remember them.

chapters.name: The Tablets of Sarranth
chapters.intro:
The Shoal keeps the drowned vaults of a city it cannot name, and has done for four hundred years, patiently, without reading a word. This year one of them can. Ilo, a young oracle of the Reading Reef, has found the tablets of Sarranth and read what his people were: the most learned city on the coast, fled into the sea from the Second Burning behind a breathing-spell, and changed by it into this.

Chief Gorrok Bluntjaw says the tablets are lies and the sea is enough. Thunn Reefbreaker, Ilo's friend, stands with Ilo. Your reef can raise creatures up to tier 2. Take Bluntjaw Reef.
chapters.text: Ilo reads the tablets of Sarranth; Chief Gorrok forbids it; the Shoal splits and Ilo's side takes Gorrok's reef.
chapters.outro:
Gorrok Bluntjaw sits on the sandbar with the lagoon on either side and asks to be read to. Ilo reads him the last tablet, the one he has not read to anyone: that the breathing-spell did not go wrong on its own. One rune of it was changed, by a shaman of the north named Skadric Whalebone, out of envy.

Gorrok is quiet for a long time. Then he says: "Then we were wronged." It is the first thing the Shoal has agreed on in four hundred years.

chapters.name: One Shoal
chapters.intro:
Mother Urrh's shoal is the last that will not follow. She says the mainland is a story, that the Shoal has forgotten for a reason, and that Ilo will get them all killed on dry sand. Sael Hookhand, her best harpooner, has read the tablets too, and comes over with his boat.

Tier 3 is open: shellbacks. From Ilo's Mudhall, take the Middle Reef between you, then break Urrh's Shoal and make the Shoal one.
chapters.text: The last shoal refuses Ilo; Sael Hookhand joins; the Shoal becomes one.
chapters.outro:
Mother Urrh kneels in the shallows and says she still thinks Ilo is wrong, and that she will come anyway, because a shoal swims together or it does not swim. The whole Shoal turns north and east, toward a coast none of them has seen and all of them remember in their bones.

Ilo keeps the tablets in a sealed shell on his chest. He has started to notice that he thinks faster than he did a year ago, and wonders whether reading does that, or whether it is the air.

chapters.name: Landfall
chapters.intro:
The Living Shore. The Red Sky war is nearly over and its leavings are here: Ashen stragglers under the brood chief Garsh Emberclaw hold the coast road, and the dead of the Pale Inheritance watch from the fens and do not interfere. Nobody on the shore knows what the Shoal is. A Concord oracle, Sister Edda Vey, comes down to the surf with a lantern that burns white near the Shoal instead of blue, and goes away again thinking.

Hold the Landing, take the empty harbour town of Shorehold on the coast road, and break Emberclaw's Camp at its northern end.
chapters.text: The Shoal makes landfall on the Living Shore and clears the Ashen stragglers from the coast.
chapters.outro:
Emberclaw's brood breaks on the shingle and the Shoal stands on the mainland. The Concord sends thanks, carefully worded, to "the people of the sea," and asks nothing about them. It has had a hard year.

Ilo reads the tablets' map against the real coast and finds the Whaleroad river where it should be, far to the north, with a glacier at its head and a cairn on the glacier. The north is where the tablets point. The north is cold. Thunn says the word as if it were a creature.

chapters.name: The Last Brood
chapters.intro:
Aldous Wren of the Concord has two broods left on the Barrow Roads, under Vrask the Twice-Eaten and Gaul Cindermouth, and not enough lances to finish them. He offers the people of the sea a share of the roads if they will fight beside him. He does not ask what they are. He does not look at them for long.

Tier 4 is open: mire crabs. Wren's lances camp in the east. Fight beside them and break both broods: Vrask's Pit in the south-west and Cindermouth in the south-east.
chapters.text: Two against two: the Shoal and Aldous Wren break the last Ashen broods on the Barrow Roads.
chapters.outro:
The broods are finished and the Concord owes the Shoal, and says so, in writing. Wren shakes Thunn's claw and does not flinch much.

"They don't remember us," Ilo says that night. "Four hundred years. We were their teachers." Sael says that makes the north very easy to reach: nobody will stop a people they cannot name. Thunn says the north is still cold.

objectives.text: Burn out the last two broods
Greyhold's Lances must not fall

chapters.name: The Price of Iron
chapters.intro:
The Shoal cannot bear the cold. On the first frost of the Barrow Roads a hundred brine-spears stiffened and died standing. The Forge makes furnace-mail that keeps a man warm on a glacier, and Ironmarshal Dask Vell, at the gates of Kharrak's outer holds, says the Forge gave the Concord a stone once and was paid a hundred years late. "We give nothing freely."

Tier 5 is open: lantern acolytes. Take Ironstair, the smiths' town on the mountain road, then Kharrak's Outer Gate and the forges behind it.
chapters.text: The Forge refuses the Shoal furnace-mail; the Shoal takes Kharrak's outer forges.
chapters.outro:
Dask Vell yields the outer holds with their forges still hot. In them are the furnace-mail patterns, and smiths who can make them, and three weeks of work before the first harness is ready for a body shaped like Thunn's.

Ilo offers to pay. Vell says the Forge will take payment when the Shoal has gone, and that the Forge will be back before then. Ilo believes him.

chapters.name: Three Weeks of Fire
chapters.intro:
Gunnra Sootmantle comes down from Kharrak Hold with the whole Forge behind her to take her furnaces back. The harness is three weeks from ready: visor, mail, greaves, run through with emberglass that holds heat the way the Shoal's blood cannot.

Hold the Upper and Lower Furnace for three weeks against every hammer-column Kharrak Hold sends up the road through Slagmouth, and the Forgewarm Harness is yours.
chapters.text: Survival: hold the Forge's furnaces for three weeks while the Forgewarm Harness is made.
chapters.outro:
On the twenty-first day the first harness comes off the anvil and Thunn puts it on and stands in the snow outside the hold for an hour, and lives, and laughs. Gunnra Sootmantle, watching from the ridge, withdraws. The Forge will remember the debt. The Forge remembers everything.

The Shoal has what it needs for the north. Ilo looks at the harness and thinks about Sarranth, which made things like this once and taught the Forge how.

objectives.text: Hold both furnace-holds through day 21
Break every hammer-column Kharrak sends

chapters.name: The Cold Road
chapters.intro:
The Iron Pass and the southern clan halls. The first snow of the year, and the Shoal walks into it in furnace-mail, and the clans under Hrodna Grimfell come out to see what is walking. Nobody in the north has asked what the fish-folk want here. Nobody has had to.

Tier 6 is open: tide maulers. Take the Pass Fort in the Iron Pass, then Grimfell's clan-hall beyond it.
chapters.text: The Shoal takes the Iron Pass and the first clan hall in the snow.
chapters.outro:
Grimfell's hall burns, and the Shoal stands around the fire with their visors up, as close as they can get. Hrodna Grimfell asks Ilo, as she is led away, what the sea people want with the clans, who have never seen the sea.

Ilo says: "Skadric Whalebone." She has never heard the name. Nobody in the north has. It is in the tablets, and the tablets are four hundred years old, and Ilo is beginning to understand what revenge on the dead looks like.

chapters.name: Who Pays the Clans
chapters.intro:
The Concord marches north with the Shoal. Aldous Wren says the clans burned Concord granaries under the red sky and the Concord has a debt to settle, and that debts are what the Concord is made of. Thane Orm Whaleroad of the shaman clan holds the northern halls, and his clan keeps a cairn on the glacier it never speaks of.

Tier 7 is open: coil serpents. Take Orm's Longhall and then Whaleroad Hall, the clan's two halls in the west, with the Concord beside you.
chapters.text: The Concord marches with the Shoal against the clans, then Aldous Wren pays the Concord's old debt and turns.
chapters.outro:
The second hall falls and Aldous Wren turns his lances on the Shoal. The clans kept the Wound shut a hundred years ago and the Concord never paid them, and it pays them now, with the Shoal.

"I am sorry," Wren says, across the snow, and he means it. "You were owed too. I only had enough for one." Ilo, who has read every history Sarranth kept, has not read one where the Concord paid anyone on time, and is not surprised, and is surprised at how much it hurts.

betrayal.text: I am sorry. You were owed too. I only had enough for one.

objectives.text: Keep Greyhold's Lances with you
Take both clan halls
Break Clan Whaleroad, and whoever stands with it

chapters.name: The Whaleroad Cairn
chapters.intro:
Nothing of the Shoal's can live on the glacier. The rivermouth camps are all the shelter there is, and the Shoal holds no town. Seer Iska Rime holds the ice above with the shaman clan's last warbands and the cairn behind her.

Tier 8 is open: trench titans. The Rivermouth Hall, Saltmere and Rimewatch are abandoned shelters along the way; Whaleroad's ice-camp guards the glacier's end. Bring Ilo to the cairn and open it.
chapters.text: Townless on the glacier, the Shoal fights up to Skadric Whalebone's cairn.
chapters.outro:
The cairn opens on bones and a carved slab, and the carving is in Sarranth's own letters, because the shaman learned them from the Sarranthi before he betrayed them. Skadric Whalebone's confession, cut by his own hand: "I changed one rune. They would have left us in the cold."

Ilo reads it to the Shoal. Nobody cheers. Thunn asks what it means. Ilo says it means the Shoal was wronged by a dead man who was wronged first, and that the north has never been warm, and that the Shoal is still cold.

objectives.text: Take back the Rivermouth Hall
Bring Ilo to the cairn at the glacier's end

chapters.name: Who Was Cold First
chapters.intro:
Kettlehall and the Hall of the Endless Feast: Ulvra Kettleborn's clans and Aldous Wren's Concord, allied on the Whaleroad, between the Shoal and the sea. There is no way home that does not go through both.

The Shoal has the Harness, the tablets and nothing else to lose. From the Rivermouth Camp, take the Whaleroad Steading on the river, then Kettlehall in the north and the Hall of the Endless Feast in the south.
chapters.text: One against two: the Shoal against the clans and the Concord, for the way home.
chapters.outro:
Kettlehall burns, and Ilo walks into the heat of it in his furnace-mail and stands there until he cannot bear it, and feels, for a moment, his skin begin to remember what it was. Then he walks back out into the cold with his people.

The Shoal goes home to the sea with the tablets of Sarranth and the Forgewarm patterns and a debt from the Concord and a debt to the Forge. It knows what it was now. Ilo has begun teaching the young ones to read. It will take a long time. The Shoal is patient. It always was.
